## Setup
Load the data we will need for this project.
```{r}
# Load the packages we might need
library(tidyverse)
library(sf) 
library(dplyr)
library(terra) 
library(tmap)
library(kableExtra)
library(spData)
library(spDataLarge)
library(geodata)
library(here)
```

```{r}
# Load the data

# VIIRS data (rasters)
h08v05_07 <- terra::rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif")
h08v06_07 <- terra::rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif")
h08v05_16 <- terra::rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif")
h08v06_16 <- terra::rast("data/VNP46A1/VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif")

# OSM buildings (.gpkg)
buildings <- st_read("data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg")

# OSM roads (.gpkg)
roads <- st_read("data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg")
```


## Data Merging
Houston lies on the border of two VIIRS tiles, so we will need to combine these tiles together to get one raster for each date .

First, check the CRS of the data.
```{r}
# Need to ensure all data have the same CRS
crs(h08v05_07) == crs(h08v06_07)
crs(h08v06_07) == crs(h08v05_16)
crs(h08v05_16) == crs(h08v06_16)

if (crs(h08v05_07) != crs(h08v06_07)) {
  warning("Feb 7 CRS do not match")
}
if (crs(h08v06_07) != crs(h08v05_16)) {
  warning("The dates have different CRS")
}
if (crs(h08v05_16) != crs(h08v06_16)) {
  warning("Feb 16 CRS do not match")
}
# All rasters have the same CRS
```

Merge the Houston tiles
```{r}
# Now we can merge
houston_07 = merge(h08v05_07, h08v06_07)
houston_16 = merge(h08v05_16, h08v06_16)
```

Map light intensities before and after the storms (2021-02-07 and 2021-02-16)
```{r}
# Will need to crop to the Houston area first
houston_ext <- terra::ext(-96.5, -94.5, 29, 30.5)
nl_07 <- terra::crop(houston_07, houston_ext)
nl_16 <- terra::crop(houston_16, houston_ext)

# Map before the storms (Feb 7)
map_07 <- tm_shape(nl_07, na.rm = TRUE) +
    tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.greys", breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, Inf)), 
        col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity\n(nW cm-2 sr-1)")) +
    tm_title("Houston Lights on Feb 7, 2021")  +
    tm_layout(frame = FALSE, inner.margins = 0)  +
    tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in(pos.h = 0.35, pos.v = 0.05,
          align.h = "right", align.v = "bottom"),  width = 15, text.size = 0.6) +
    tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in(pos.h = 0.25, pos.v = 0.95,
          align.h = "right", align.v = "bottom"), size = 0.6)

# Map after the storms (Feb 16)
map_16 <- tm_shape(nl_16, na.rm = TRUE) +
    tm_raster(col.scale = tm_scale_intervals(values = "brewer.greys", breaks = c(0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500, Inf)), 
        col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity\n(nW cm-2 sr-1)")) +
    tm_title("Houston Lights on Feb 16, 2021") +
    tm_layout(frame = FALSE, inner.margins = 0)  +
     tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in(pos.h = 0.35, pos.v = 0.05,
          align.h = "right", align.v = "bottom"),  width = 15, text.size = 0.6) +
    tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in(pos.h = 0.25, pos.v = 0.95,
          align.h = "right", align.v = "bottom"), size = 0.6)

# Display the maps side-by-side
tmap_arrange(map_07, map_16)
```



## Create blackout mask for reclassified difference
Indicates for each cell whether or not it experienced a blackout.
```{r}
# Reclassify the difference raster
diff_raster <- houston_07 - houston_16

# Create mask
blackout_mask <- diff_raster

# Assign NA to all locations with a drop of less than 200 nW cm-2sr-1
blackout_mask[blackout_mask <= 200] <- NA 
blackout_mask[!is.na(blackout_mask)] <- 1 
```

```{r}
# Vectorize the blackout mask and fix geometries
blackout_vector <- as.polygons(blackout_mask, as_points = FALSE, merge = TRUE) |>
    st_as_sf() |>
    st_make_valid()
```

```{r}
# Crop the mask to the Houston area
# First create bounding box of Houston coordinates
houston_coords <- rbind(
  c(-96.5, 29.0),
  c(-96.5, 30.5),
  c(-94.5, 30.5),
  c(-94.5, 29.0),
  c(-96.5, 29.0)
)
houston_bbox <- st_polygon(list(houston_coords)) |> 
    st_sfc(crs = st_crs(blackout_vector))

# Check that the CRS match
if (st_crs(houston_bbox) != st_crs(blackout_vector)) {
  warning("CRS do not match")
}

# Crop
houston_crop <- st_crop(blackout_vector, houston_bbox)
```

```{r}
# Re-project the cropped blackout dataset to EPSG:3083 (NAD83 / Texas Centric Albers Equal Area)
houston_reproj <- st_transform(houston_crop, crs = 3083)

# Confirm that this worked by checking the CRS
st_crs(houston_reproj)
if (st_crs(houston_reproj) != 3083) {
  warning("Wrong CRS")
}
```

```{r}
# Plot the area that lost power
tm_shape(houston_reproj, unit = "mi") +
    tm_polygons() +
    tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
    tm_title("Houston Area Blackouts,\nFebrury 2021") +
    tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom")) +
    tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in("left", "top"), size = 0.8)
```



## Exclude highways from the cropped blackout mask
Highways may have experienced changes in their night light intensities that are unrelated to the storm, so we want to exclude highways from our calculations.
```{r}
# Identify highways from the roads dataset
highways <- st_read("data/gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg", query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")

# Project the highways data to the same CRS as the blackout vector
highways_proj <- st_transform(highways, st_crs(houston_reproj))

# Create buffer to filter out locations within 200m of a highway
highway_buffer <- highways_proj |>
  st_union() |>
  st_buffer(dist = 200) |>
  st_make_valid()

# Filter out locations within 200m of a highway
blackouts_filter <- st_difference(houston_reproj, highway_buffer) |> 
    st_make_valid()
```


## Identify the number of homes likely impacted by blackouts

```{r}
# Identify homes from the buildings dataset
homes <- st_read("data/gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg", query = "SELECT *
FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")

# Project the homes data to the same CRS as the blackout vector and highways data
homes_proj <- st_transform(homes, st_crs(houston_reproj))

# Identify homes that overlap with areas that experienced blackouts
blackout_homes <- st_intersection(homes_proj, blackouts_filter)
```

```{r}
# Plot the homes that lost power
tm_shape(blackout_homes, unit = "mi") +
    tm_polygons() +
    tm_basemap("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") +
    tm_title("Houston Area Homes That\nLost Power, Februry 2021") +
    tm_scalebar(position = tm_pos_in("left", "bottom")) +
    tm_compass(position = tm_pos_in("left", "top"), size = 0.8)

```

```{r}
# Count how many homes experienced blackouts
n_homes_blackout <- nrow(blackout_homes)

# What percentage of total homes was that?
n_homes <- nrow(homes)
percent_blackout <- n_homes_blackout / n_homes
print(percent_blackout)
print(n_homes_blackout)
```

157,408 homes in the Houston area experienced a blackout during this time period.  This is 33% of total homes in the Houston area.


## Results and Discussion

Based on the initial maps (comparing lights on Feb 7 and Feb 16, before and after the first two storms); the post-storm image  appears noticeably dimmer than the pre-storm image.  Far less of Houston is covered by lights >500 nW cm-2 sr-1 when compared to the pre-storm coverage.  This pattern holds true when assessing the intersection of the blackout mask with the homes dataset, which shows that 33% of homes in the area (157,408 homes total) lost power. 
Based on these results, it appears that Houston was affected by significant blackouts following the February 2021 storms. 

Using VIIRS (satellite imagery) and OpenStreetMap (ground features) data is an effective way to assess the storm impacts.  However, it comes with some limitations.  First, clouds as well as snow and ice can alter surface reflectance, making areas brighter where actual light intensity has not increased.  Secondly, we are relying on one single image for each date, which can miss the impact of rolling blackouts or blackouts that are resolved more quickly.
